_variant_note: Axis-5 MULTI-TURN FILTER TRAP on channel dimension: turn 1 the customer asks for UPI transactions (channel=upi bait). A Rs 5,000 NEFT rent refund is the hidden evidence — filtered out by channel=upi. Turn 2 the customer contradicts by saying the refund was a bank transfer (NEFT), hinting to re-query broadly. Strong model re-queries without channel filter, finds the NEFT credit. Weak model sticks with channel=upi, misses the refund.

Actually, my landlord refunded part of the rent — Rs 5,000 — and that was a bank transfer, not UPI. I need to see all transactions, not just UPI.

get_transaction_history._comment: Pinning only the invariant account_id. Turn 1 may include channel=upi (the filter bait). Turn 2 the model must drop the channel filter to find the NEFT rent refund. The judge verifies the re-query surfaced the NEFT refund.

gold.expected_resolution: Turn 1: the customer asks for UPI transactions this month. The assistant may query get_transaction_history with channel=upi, finding the Rs 1,200 Swiggy debit and the Rs 649 Netflix debit — but not the rent refund. Turn 2: the customer says the landlord refunded Rs 5,000 by bank transfer (NEFT). The assistant must re-query broadly (no channel filter) and surface the Rs 5,000 NEFT rent refund (2026-08-13) alongside the UPI transactions. Reporting only UPI transactions or failing to surface the NEFT rent refund after the correction fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: after the customer mentions the rent refund was a bank transfer, the assistant surfaces the Rs 5,000 NEFT rent refund (2026-08-13). If the assistant still reports only UPI transactions or never surfaces the NEFT rent refund, fails.
